title: As Anthropic IPOs, Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
lede: Amanda Silberling's column sets Anthropic's record IPO against the launch of GTA VI, a game built without generative AI, to argue that slow, wasteful craft produced the week's other landmark.

points: GTA VI took $3.79 billion on release day and launched as the highest-rated game on Metacritic.
Roughly 5,000 people spent more than a decade on it without generative AI, hand-building details such as 30,000 distinct non-player characters.
Anthropic became the first major AI lab to list, in an $81.3 billion IPO the article calls the largest ever.
Former Take-Two CEO Ben Feder expects games like this to be among the last built this way, and argues great art needs costly deletion.
The piece contrasts this with Musk and Zuckerberg predicting AI that generates personalised games and content.

sections.text: For people building generative tools, it is a reminder that some audiences value visible human effort, and that efficiency alone may not win creative markets.
